value.name: Sacramento Municipal Utility District (SMUD)
value.notes: SMUD is a vertically-integrated municipal utility — it generates/procures and delivers its own power rather than sitting alongside a separate CCA, consistent with the pattern already established for other SMUD-territory records this session.

permit_authority.value: City of Citrus Heights Community Development Department

interconnection_url.notes: SMUD's own solar hub page, which the city's page links to for the required 'SMUD interconnection pre-approval' step and which itself includes an 'Interconnection process' FAQ topic.

value.name: My Energy Optimizer Partner+
value.description: SMUD's own battery storage incentive program (separate from the CPUC/IOU-administered SGIP, which does not apply to SMUD customers as a municipal utility outside CPUC jurisdiction). One-time enrollment incentive of up to $10,000 per household ($500/kWh minus a 20% holdback) for new battery energy storage system customers who enroll within 90 days of receiving Permission to Operate (PTO) from SMUD. Ongoing quarterly incentives are currently only available for Tesla batteries ($110 for 1 battery, $220 for 2, $330 for 3+); other eligible brands (Eguana, Enphase, Franklin, SolarEdge, Sonnen) receive only the one-time enrollment incentive at this time.
value.eligibility: SMUD residential customers with a battery storage unit installed at their home who participate in SMUD's Solar and Storage Rate (SSR). Individual rental units are currently ineligible; multifamily homes are eligible with the same tenant restrictions. MED Rate customers are not eligible.
